title: Repeat speculations by the same speaker
note: One speculation per speaker per work: when a speaker has speculations in several works, the one with the widest scope of change counts, ties to the earliest. The others are kept here, out of every count and reading. Distinct speculations within one work (scenarios, concept cards, a workshop's statements) all count.

speculations.text: The moving picture art will largely supplement the art of printing.
speculations.speaker: Inventor
speculations.source: Frank Parker Hulette, interview with Thomas Edison, Moving Picture World, 22 July 1911, pp. 104–105. Compiled in “Thomas Edison’s Education Predictions”, muninn.net.

speculations.text: I believe that the motion picture is destined to revolutionize our educational system and that in a few years it will supplant largely, if not entirely, the use of textbooks.
speculations.speaker: Inventor
speculations.source: Hugh Weir, “The Story of the Motion Picture”, McClure’s 54, November 1922, p. 85; quoted in Cuban (1986).
speculations.verify: Full wording taken from secondary sources; check against McClure’s.

speculations.text: Textbooks as the principal medium of teaching will be as obsolete as the horse and carriage are now.
speculations.speaker: Inventor
speculations.source: Hugh Weir, “What Edison Would Like to Do with the Movies”, Collier’s 75, 21 February 1925, pp. 20–21. Compiled in muninn.net (as above).

speculations.text: If you just took the next 18 months, the AIs will come in as a teacher’s aide and give feedback on writing. … The AIs will get to that ability, to be as good a tutor as any human ever could.
speculations.speaker: Company
speculations.source: Bill Gates, ASU+GSV Summit, San Diego, April 2023; reported in CNBC, 22 April 2023.
